If the parser read less than expected (end < start), the code computes diff = start - end and calls Stream_Seek(s, diff) to skip forward, but the earlier check `if (start > end)` returns FALSE in that case, so the skip branch is unreachable; conversely when end > start (parser over-read), diff underflows as size_t and the logic is wrong. The intended check should compare end against start and seek by (start - end) only when end < start. This can cause incorrect stream positioning/desynchronization on malformed secondary orders.

Also bytes is not clamped to the buffer size, so repeated descriptors can overflow the 64-byte stack buffer.
